title: Unit – 1 : Session – 2 : SLO – 2 | Abstraction & Specification
sections: 1) interface Shape { double area(); }  class Circle implements Shape { double r; Circle(double r){this.r=r;} public double area(){ return Math.PI*r*r; } }  Use: Shape s = new Circle(2); System.out.println(s.area());

2) Abstraction via access modifiers: class Account { private double balance; // hidden data  public void deposit(double amt){ if(amt>0) balance += amt; }  public double getBalance(){ return balance; } } — private hides the internal state; public methods expose only controlled operations.

3) Real-world analogy: driving a car — the driver uses the steering wheel, pedals and gear lever (public interface) without knowing the engine, transmission or fuel-injection details (private implementation). Similarly, a Java class exposes public methods while hiding fields and internal logic, so users interact with 'what' it does, not 'how' it does it.
